coordinates.locator: OSM building footprint centroid for the PHENIX/sPHENIX hall (buildings 1008/1008A), identified against BNL's central campus map
coordinates.note: Refinement from the campus-wide ROR point (1.5 km precision) to the PHENIX/sPHENIX experimental hall footprint at RHIC interaction point 8. Previous record: campus point 40.86954, -72.88677 at 1500 m precision, sources ['src:bnl-rhic-complex-page']; moved 670 m (2026-09-21).

name: RHIC Interaction Point 8 (PHENIX / sPHENIX experimental hall)
notes: This hall housed PHENIX from RHIC's first collisions in 2000, then its successor sPHENIX; both STAR and sPHENIX were the two active RHIC detectors named in the official announcement of RHIC's final run on 2026-02-06 (src:heavy-ions-rhic-final-collisions-2026: 'crashed into one another ... inside the STAR and sPHENIX detectors').

Secondary sources (search-engine summaries of physics papers, not checked against the papers) describe this as RHIC's 8 o'clock interaction point. That clock-position label is not recorded as a sourced fact because no primary or official source consulted states it.

summary.plain: The experimental hall on the RHIC particle-collider ring at Brookhaven National Laboratory that housed the PHENIX detector and later its successor, sPHENIX.
summary.technical: One of the two interaction-region halls that remained active on the Relativistic Heavy Ion Collider ring at Brookhaven National Laboratory; occupied first by the PHENIX detector and later by its successor sPHENIX, through RHIC's final run in 2026. The recorded point is the centroid of the hall's building footprint as traced in OpenStreetMap (about 100 m precision), not a geodetic survey point.
